text:
RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 35

The all-male panel is context, not evidence. It's common in municipal government and proves nothing on its own — plenty of such panels hire women. Raised as your main argument, it sounds speculative and puts people on the defensive.

Your stronger facts are concrete: a credential and experience gap on paper, and a two-week silence on a reasonable request for written reasons. Pursue those first. Escalate the unanswered request in writing to HR, citing any policy or statutory right to reasons.

Panel composition becomes relevant later — if the reasons you receive are vague, shift criteria, or lean on subjective "fit." Then it's one data point in a pattern, which is far more persuasive than an opening accusation.
